description:
About the Position

Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) invites applications for a PhD position on spatiotemporal light generation with frequency-gradient metasurfaces. The project explores engineered metasurfaces that imprint controlled frequency gradients on ultrashort optical pulses, enabling ultrafast beam steering, temporal focusing and self-torque light beams. The doctoral candidate will design, fabricate and characterise these structures and study how spatiotemporal control of light opens new regimes for ultrafast optics and nano-optical applications.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral appointment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement, embedded in TU/e's nano-optics research environment with access to advanced cleanroom fabrication and ultrafast photonics laboratories. The work combines electromagnetic simulation, nanofabrication and optical experiments, and connects to a broader research agenda on structured light and metasurface photonics with international collaboration partners.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in physics, photonics or electrical engineering, with a solid background in optics and wave physics. Experience with ultrafast lasers, metasurface design, cleanroom fabrication or optical characterisation is an advantage. Applications are submitted through TU/e's Varbi recruitment system with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter; selection weighs academic record, research experience and fit with the project.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD employment under the CAO-NU agreement
  • Frequency-gradient metasurfaces for spatiotemporal light control
  • Ultrafast beam steering, temporal focusing and self-torque
  • Simulation, nanofabrication and ultrafast optical experiments
  • Advanced cleanroom and ultrafast photonics laboratories
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system
